statements.impact_statement: The bug is in the access-point side of 802.11w (hostapd code, built into wpa_supplicant only for AP/P2P-GO mode). beast-net's only wpa_supplicant configuration is generated by wpa_config() (beastnet/python/beastnet/wifi.py:182-221): one station network block with key_mgmt NONE, OWE, WPA-PSK and/or SAE, never mode=2 or P2P, so wpa_supplicant never acts as an access point.

Heap overflow in awk (editors/awk.c next_token). beast-net ships no link for awk (build/beastnet/userland.list 'exclude usr/*bin/...', which build/beastnet/mkinitrd.py:385 also applies to busybox applet links), so the code is in /usr/bin/busybox but never runs: /init, udhcpc.script, mdev.conf and the app only run the programs listed in beastnet/runtime.json 'binaries' and never call 'busybox <applet>', and busybox sh has no standalone-applet mode (with the shipped binary, a command without a link is 'not found').

statements.action_statement: Disk tools run 'lvm' (pvs, vgs, lvs and vgchange -ay, beastnet/python/beastnet/disks) on attached disks, so a crafted deeply nested LVM metadata area can exhaust the stack of that one lvm process (denial of service of LVM discovery; the report names no memory corruption). Each lvm call is a separate short-lived process, so beast-net itself keeps running and reports the failed command. Wait for Ubuntu's fix (2.03.31-2ubuntu3 is the newest in Ubuntu 26.04 and 26.10); when it is published, re-run build/beastnet/lock.py, make build, make e2e and re-scan.

wpas_handle_robust_av_scs_recv_action (robust_av.c) returns at its first check unless wpa_s->ongoing_scs_req is set; that flag is set only by wpas_send_scs_req, whose only caller is the 'SCS' control-interface command (hostap 2.11 ctrl_iface.c). beast-net's control-socket client (beastnet/python/beastnet/wifi.py WpaCtrl) sends only ATTACH and STATUS, wpa_cli is never run, and the socket is in the root-only /run/beastnet/wpa, so an AP's SCS response frame is dropped before the vulnerable code.

statements.action_statement: Python 3.14.4's ssl module lacks the denylist of known-compromised certificates. beast-net verifies HTTPS downloads against the Ubuntu CA bundle, so only a stolen key of a certificate that still validates for the contacted host could be abused. Ubuntu has no fix in 26.04 (the 26.10 python 3.14.8 needs OpenSSL 4 and glibc 2.44, which this helper does not carry). When Ubuntu publishes a fix for 26.04, re-run build/beastnet/lock.py, make build, make e2e and re-scan.
